name_translation: The Yoga of Sovereign Science and Sovereign Secret

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे |
ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् || १ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे |
ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
idaṃ tu te guhyatamaṃ pravakṣyāmyanasūyave |
jñānaṃ vijñānasahitaṃ yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt || 1 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; idam—this; tu—further; te—unto you; guhya-tamam—the most confidential; pravakṣyāmi—I shall declare; anasūyave—to the non-envious; jñānam—knowledge; vijñāna-sahitam—accompanied by realized experiential wisdom; yat jñātvā—knowing which; mokṣyase—you shall be liberated; aśubhāt—from inauspiciousness/mortal bondage.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: To you who are non-envious, I shall now impart this most confidential knowledge (Guhyatama) together with direct realization (Vijnana), knowing which you shall be liberated from all inauspicious material bondage.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna opens Chapter 9 by qualifying Arjuna as 'Anasuyave'—free from the taint of envy, pride, and fault-finding. Because Arjuna's heart is purely receptive and non-envious, the Lord reveals the most profound and confidential secret of divine existence (Guhyatama Jnana), which combines theoretical wisdom with direct experiential perception (Vijnana), conferring complete liberation from the miseries of material transmigration (Ashubhat).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् |
प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम् || २ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् |
प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम् || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
rājavidyā rājaguhyaṃ pavitramidamuttamam |
pratyakṣāvagamaṃ dharmyaṃ susukhaṃ kartumavyayam || 2 ||
verses.word_meanings: rāja-vidyā—the sovereign science; rāja-guhyam—the sovereign secret; pavitram—purifier; idam—this; uttamam—supreme; pratyakṣa-avagamam—directly perceivable by direct realization; dharmyam—in accord with righteousness; su-sukham—supremely joyful; kartum—to practice; avyayam—imperishable, eternal.
verses.translation: This is the sovereign science, the sovereign secret, supreme in purifying power, directly perceivable through experiential realization, harmonious with righteous virtue (Dharma), very joyful to practice, and imperishable.
verses.meaning: The Lord glorifies this supreme knowledge with eight sublime attributes: It is Raja Vidya (the king of sciences), Raja Guhya (the king of secrets), Pavitram Uttamam (the highest purifier of the heart), Pratyakshavagamam (directly realizable through personal spiritual experience), Dharmyam (the eternal essence of righteousness), Susukham Kartum (supremely joyful to perform), and Avyayam (imperishable, bringing everlasting fruits).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप |
अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि || ३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप |
अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya parantapa |
aprāpya māṃ nivartante mṛtyusaṃsāravartmani || 3 ||
verses.word_meanings: aśraddadhānāḥ—those lacking faith; puruṣāḥ—persons; dharmasya asya—in this sacred dharma; parantapa—O chastiser of foes; aprāpya—without attaining; mām—Me; nivartante—they return; mṛtyu-saṃsāra-vartmani—to the path of the world of death and transmigration.
verses.translation: Those who lack faith in this sacred dharma, O chastiser of foes (Arjuna), failing to attain Me, return to the perpetual path of death and rebirth in the mortal world.
verses.meaning: Shraddha (firm, loving faith founded on spiritual conviction) is the prerequisite for realizing this sovereign secret. Without faith, people remain bound by cynical materialism and sense cravings, drifting endlessly along the wheel of samsara (Mrityu-samsara-vartma) without ever experiencing the divine bliss of union with the Supreme.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना |
मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः || ४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना |
मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mayā tatamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagadavyaktamūrtinā |
matsthāni sarvabhūtāni na cāhaṃ teṣvavasthitaḥ || 4 ||
verses.word_meanings: mayā—by Me; tatam—is pervaded; idam—this; sarvam—all; jagat—universe; avyakta-mūrtinā—by My unmanifest form; mat-sthāni—residing in Me; sarva-bhūtāni—all living entities; na—not; ca—and; aham—I; teṣu—in them; avasthitaḥ—contained/limited.
verses.translation: By Me in My unmanifest form (Avyakta-murti), this entire universe is pervaded. All living beings abide in Me, but I am not contained in them.
verses.meaning: A monumental philosophical revelation of Achintya Bhedabheda (inconceivable simultaneous oneness and difference). Sri Krishna permeates the entire cosmos with His unmanifest divine energy; every created entity rests within His infinite conscious being (Mat-sthani sarva-bhutani). Yet, as the transcendent Supreme Sovereign, He is never limited, contained, or modified by finite creation (Na chaham teshv avasthitah).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् |
भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः || ५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् |
भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
na ca matsthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogamaiśvaram |
bhūtabhṛnna ca bhūtastho mamātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ || 5 ||
verses.word_meanings: na ca—and nor; mat-sthāni—residing in Me (materially); bhūtāni—created beings; paśya—behold; me—My; yogam aiśvaram—divine sovereign yoga/mystery; bhūta-bhṛt—the sustainer of beings; na ca—and yet not; bhūta-sthaḥ—abiding in matter; mama ātmā—My Self; bhūta-bhāvanaḥ—the source/creator of beings.
verses.translation: And yet, created beings do not abide in Me in a material, limiting sense—behold My sovereign divine mystery (Yogam Aishvaram)! As the Creator and Sustainer of all beings, My Self does not abide in them as a material object.
verses.meaning: The Lord deepens the paradox to purify Arjuna's understanding from spatial and material concepts. Just as thoughts exist in consciousness without physically weighting down the mind, all beings emerge from, are sustained by, and dissolve into the Divine without affecting His absolute independence, purity, and transcendence.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यथाकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् |
तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय || ६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यथाकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् |
तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yathākāśasthito nityaṃ vāyuḥ sarvatrago mahān |
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni matsthānītyupadhāraya || 6 ||
verses.word_meanings: yathā—just as; ākāśa-sthitaḥ—abiding in space (ether); nityam—always; vāyuḥ—the wind; sarvatra-gaḥ—moving everywhere; mahān—the mighty; tathā—similarly; sarvāṇi bhūtāni—all created beings; mat-sthāni—abide in Me; iti—thus; upadhāraya—understand.
verses.translation: Understand that just as the mighty wind, blowing everywhere, always rests within space (Akasha), so do all created beings abide in Me.
verses.meaning: A sublime Vedic analogy: Space (Akasha) contains the mighty, ever-moving wind without clinging to it or being displaced by it. Similarly, the all-pervading Supreme Consciousness holds all cosmic beings, galaxies, and elements within Himself without ever being tainted, constrained, or agitated by their finite actions.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम् |
कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम् || ७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम् |
कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम् || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sarvabhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṃ yānti māmikām |
kalpakṣaye punastāni kalpādau visṛjāmyaham || 7 ||
verses.word_meanings: sarva-bhūtāni—all living entities; kaunteya—O son of Kunti; prakṛtim—into material nature; yānti—enter; māmikām—My; kalpa-kṣaye—at the end of a Kalpa (cosmic age); punaḥ—again; tāni—them; kalpa-ādau—at the beginning of a Kalpa; visṛjāmi—project/create; aham—I.
verses.translation: All created beings, O son of Kunti, enter into My material nature (Prakriti) at the end of a cosmic cycle (Kalpa-kshaye); and at the beginning of the next cycle, I emanate them again.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna describes the grand cosmic cycle of manifestation and dissolution. At the end of Brahma's day (Kalpa-kshaya), the diverse forms of all living entities dissolve back into Krishna's primordial unmanifest material nature (Mamikam Prakritim). When a new cosmic dawn arrives (Kalpadau), the Lord projects them once more according to their stored karmic impressions.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः |
भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात् || ८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः |
भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात् || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
prakṛtiṃ svāmavaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ |
bhūtagrāmamimaṃ kṛtsnamavaśaṃ prakṛtervaśāt || 8 ||
verses.word_meanings: prakṛtim—material nature; svām—My own; avaṣṭabhya—presiding over/animating; visṛjāmi—I emanate/project; punaḥ punaḥ—again and again; bhūta-grāmam—multitude of living beings; imam—this; kṛtsnam—all; avaśam—helpless; prakṛteḥ vaśāt—under the control of material nature.
verses.translation: Animating My own material nature (Prakriti), I project again and again this entire multitude of beings, which is helpless under the sway of nature's modes (Gunas).
verses.meaning: Material nature is not an independent creator; it is animated and energized by the Supreme Lord. Under the influence of their past karmic conditioning and the three modes of nature (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas), souls are born helplessly (Avasham) into suitable material forms cycle after cycle.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय |
उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु || ९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय |
उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
na ca māṃ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya |
udāsīnavadāsīnamasaktaṃ teṣu karmasu || 9 ||
verses.word_meanings: na ca—and nor; mām—Me; tāni karmāṇi—those cosmic activities; nibadhnanti—bind; dhanañjaya—O conqueror of wealth (Arjuna); udāsīnavat—as if neutral/unconcerned; āsīnam—seated; asaktam—unattached; teṣu karmasu—in those actions.
verses.translation: And these cosmic activities do not bind Me, O Dhananjaya, situated as I am like one unconcerned and detached from all these actions.
verses.meaning: Unlike mortal beings whose actions generate binding karma due to ego, desire, and attachment, the Supreme Lord remains ever untouched, unattached (Asaktam), and seated like an impartial, transcendental witness (Udasinavat) above the cosmic play.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मयाध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम् |
हेतुनानेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते || १० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मयाध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम् |
हेतुनानेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacarācaram |
hetunānena kaunteya jagadviparivartate || 10 ||
verses.word_meanings: mayā adhyakṣeṇa—under My supervision/presidency; prakṛtiḥ—material nature; sūyate—produces; sa-cara-acaram—moving and unmoving; hetunā anena—by this cause; kaunteya—O son of Kunti; jagat—the universe; viparivartate—revolves in cycles.
verses.translation: Under My divine superintendence, material nature (Prakriti) produces all things moving and unmoving; by this cause, O son of Kunti, the cosmic wheel revolves.
verses.meaning: A pivotal verse clarifying cosmic causality: Prakriti (matter) is not an unconscious, self-evolving machine; it produces the diverse moving (animate) and unmoving (inanimate) creation under the conscious supervision and will of Sri Krishna (Mayadhyakshena). The Lord is the supreme overseer and efficient cause behind cosmic evolution and dissolution.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम् |
परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम् || ११ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम् |
परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम् || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
avajānanti māṃ mūḍhā mānuṣīṃ tanumāśritam |
paraṃ bhāvamajānanto mama bhūtamaheśvaram || 11 ||
verses.word_meanings: avajānanti—deride/disregard; mām—Me; mūḍhāḥ—foolish persons; mānuṣīm tanum—a human form; āśritam—assuming/descending into; param bhāvam—supreme transcendental nature; ajānantaḥ—not knowing; mama—My; bhūta-mahā-īśvaram—the Great Lord of all beings.
verses.translation: Fools deride Me when I descend in a human form, ignorant of My supreme, transcendental nature as the Great Lord of all beings.
verses.meaning: Deluded persons lacking spiritual insight judge the Avatar of the Supreme Lord by external physical appearance alone. Unaware of His transcendental sovereignty as Bhuta-Maheshvaram (the Supreme Master of all cosmic existence), they mistakenly perceive Him as an ordinary mortal, blinding themselves to divine grace.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः |
राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः || १२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः |
राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
moghāśā moghakarmāṇo moghajñānā vicetasaḥ |
rākṣasīmāsurīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ śritāḥ || 12 ||
verses.word_meanings: moghāśāḥ—of vain hopes; mogha-karmāṇaḥ—of baffled/fruitless actions; mogha-jñānāḥ—of vain/useless knowledge; vicetasaḥ—deluded/bewildered; rākṣasīm—fiendish/monstrous; āsurīm—demoniac/atheistic; ca eva—and surely; prakṛtim—nature; mohinīm—deluding; śritāḥ—taking shelter of.
verses.translation: Possessed of vain hopes, vain actions, and vain knowledge, devoid of true discrimination, they take shelter of the delusive, demoniac and fiendish nature.
verses.meaning: Those who reject the Divine Reality fall prey to Asuric (egoic, materialistic) and Rakshasic (cruel, destructive) mentalities. Because their desires and endeavors are alienated from the cosmic Truth, their hopes are ultimately frustrated (Moghasha), their labors bear empty fruit (Moghakarma), and their secular knowledge remains hollow (Moghajnana).

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः |
भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम् || १३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः |
भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम् || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mahātmānastu māṃ pārtha daivīṃ prakṛtimāśritāḥ |
bhajantyananyamanaso jñātvā bhūtādimavyayam || 13 ||
verses.word_meanings: mahātmānaḥ—the great-souled ones; tu—but; mām—Me; pārtha—O son of Pritha; daivīm prakṛtim—divine spiritual nature; āśritāḥ—having taken refuge in; bhajanti—worship/adore; ananya-manasaḥ—with undivided mind; jñātvā—knowing; bhūta-ādim—the primeval origin of all beings; avyayam—the imperishable/inexhaustible.
verses.translation: But the great-souled ones (Mahatmas), O Partha, taking refuge in the divine spiritual nature (Daivi Prakriti), worship Me with undivided hearts, knowing Me as the imperishable source of all creation.
verses.meaning: In contrast to the deluded, the Mahatmas (noble, awakened souls) cultivate Sattvic and divine virtues—humility, compassion, self-restraint, and truthfulness. Realizing Sri Krishna as Bhutadi (the primeval origin of all existence) and Avyaya (inexhaustible and imperishable), they pour their heart's devotion exclusively into Him (Ananya-manasa).

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः |
नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते || १४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः |
नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
satataṃ kīrtayanto māṃ yatantaśca dṛḍhavratāḥ |
namasyantaśca māṃ bhaktyā nityayuktā upāsate || 14 ||
verses.word_meanings: satatam—always; kīrtayantaḥ—glorifying/singing praises of; mām—Me; yatantaḥ ca—and striving with effort; dṛḍha-vratāḥ—with steadfast/firm vows; namasyantaḥ ca—and offering obeisances; mām—unto Me; bhaktyā—with devotion; nitya-yuktāḥ—perpetually united; upāsate—they worship.
verses.translation: Always singing My divine glories, striving with determined vows, and bowing down to Me in heartfelt devotion, ever united with Me, they worship Me.
verses.meaning: The daily devotional lifestyle of true bhaktas: Through constant chanting of the Lord's holy names and glories (Kirtana), steadfast self-discipline (Dridhavrata), and reverent surrender (Namaskara), these devotees remain in unbroken communion with Krishna with deep spiritual ecstasy.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते |
एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम् || १५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते |
एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम् || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
jñānayajñena cāpyanye yajanto māmupāsate |
ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvatomukham || 15 ||
verses.word_meanings: jñāna-yajñena—by the sacrifice of knowledge; ca api—and also; anye—others; yajantaḥ—worshiping/sacrificing; mām—Me; upāsate—worship; ekatvena—in non-dual oneness; pṛthaktvena—in manifold diversity; bahudhā—in many ways; viśvataḥ-mukham—facing in all directions/the Universal Form.
verses.translation: Others also worship Me through the sacrifice of knowledge (Jnana-Yajna)—perceiving Me in non-dual unity (Ekatvena), in diversity (Prithaktvena), and as the Cosmic Form facing in all directions (Vishvatomukham).
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna acknowledges the diverse approaches of seekers on the path of Jnana. Some meditate on the Absolute as non-dual oneness (Advaita/Ekatva); others adore the Divine as manifesting through distinct cosmic energies and forms (Prithaktva); while others perceive the Lord as the all-encompassing Cosmic Person (Vishvatomukha) present everywhere.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाहमहमौषधम् |
मन्त्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम् || १६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाहमहमौषधम् |
मन्त्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम् || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ahaṃ kraturahaṃ yajñaḥ svadhāhamahamauṣadham |
mantro'hamahamevājyamahamagnirahaṃ hutam || 16 ||
verses.word_meanings: aham—I am; kratuḥ—the Vedic ritual; aham—I am; yajñaḥ—the sacrifice; svadhā—the ancestral offering; aham—I am; aham—I am; auṣadham—healing herb/food; mantraḥ—the sacred chant; aham—I am; aham eva—I alone am; ājyam—clarified butter (ghee); aham—I am; agniḥ—the fire; aham—I am; hutam—the oblation/offering.
verses.translation: I am the Vedic ritual (Kratu), I am the sacred sacrifice (Yajna), I am the ancestral oblation (Svadha), I am the healing medicinal herb, I am the sacred chant (Mantra), I am the clarified butter (Ajya), I am the consecrated fire (Agni), and I am the act of offering (Hutam).
verses.meaning: The Supreme Lord is the total reality underlying all sacred rituals: He is the formal Vedic ceremony, the inner attitude of sacrifice, the sacred food offered to ancestors, the botanical nourishment, the vibration of sacred sound, the fuel and ghee, the blazing sacrificial flame, and the offering itself. Nothing exists outside Him.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पिताहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः |
वेद्यं पवित्रमोङ्कार ऋक्साम यजुरेव च || १७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पिताहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः |
वेद्यं पवित्रमोङ्कार ऋक्साम यजुरेव च || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
pitāhamasya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ |
vedyaṃ pavitramoṅkāra ṛksāma yajureva ca || 17 ||
verses.word_meanings: pitā—the Father; aham—I am; asya jagataḥ—of this universe; mātā—the Mother; dhātā—the Sustainer/Dispenser; pitāmahaḥ—the Grandfather; vedyam—the object to be known; pavitram—the purifier; oṅkāraḥ—the sacred syllable OM; ṛk—the Rig Veda; sāma—the Sama Veda; yajuḥ—the Yajur Veda; eva ca—and also.
verses.translation: I am the Father of this universe, the Mother, the Sustainer, and the Grandfather. I am the Object of Knowledge, the Sacred Purifier, the Syllable OM, and the Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna reveals His intimate, loving cosmic relationship with creation: He is both the procreative Father and the nurturing Mother of all life, the dispenser of karma (Dhata), and the primeval ancestor (Pitamaha). He is the ultimate goal of scriptural revelation, the syllable OM, and the sacred hymns of the Vedas.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् |
प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् || १८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् |
प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
gatirbhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṃ suhṛt |
prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṃ nidhānaṃ bījamavyayam || 18 ||
verses.word_meanings: gatiḥ—the supreme goal; bhartā—the sustainer; prabhuḥ—the master; sākṣī—the witness; nivāsaḥ—the dwelling place/abode; śaraṇam—the refuge; suhṛt—the dear friend; prabhavaḥ—the origin/creation; pralayaḥ—the dissolution; sthānam—the foundation; nidhānam—the treasure-house/resting place; bījam avyayam—the imperishable seed.
verses.translation: I am the Supreme Goal, the Sustainer, the Sovereign Master, the Witness, the Abode, the Refuge, and the Dearest Friend. I am the Creation, the Dissolution, the Foundation, the Resting Place, and the Imperishable Seed.
verses.meaning: A breathtaking verse encapsulating the personal and cosmic nature of God. Krishna is Gati (the ultimate destiny), Bharta (the provider), Prabhu (the supreme ruler), Sakshi (the impartial inner witness), Nivasa (the home of all consciousness), Sharanam (the unshakeable shelter), and Suhrit (the unconditional, selflessly loving friend of every creature).

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च |
अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन || १९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च |
अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tapāmyahamahaṃ varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmyutsṛjāmi ca |
amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuśca sadasaccāhamarjuna || 19 ||
verses.word_meanings: tapāmi—radiate heat; aham—I; aham—I; varṣam—rain; nigṛhṇāmi—withhold; utsṛjāmi—send forth; ca—and; amṛtam—immortality; ca eva—and indeed; mṛtyuḥ ca—and death; sat—existence/manifest reality; asat—non-existence/unmanifest; ca—and; aham—I am; arjuna—O Arjuna.
verses.translation: I radiate heat as the sun, I withhold and send forth the rain; I am immortality as well as death; and I am both being (Sat) and non-being (Asat), O Arjuna!
verses.meaning: The Lord controls the cosmic forces: through the sun He warms the earth, and through atmospheric currents He releases or holds back life-giving monsoon rains. Metaphysically, He is Amrita (the nectar of eternal life) and Mrityu (physical mortality), Sat (manifest gross reality) and Asat (unmanifest subtle potentiality).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापा
यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते |
ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोक-
मश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान् || २० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापा
यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते |
ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोक-
मश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान् || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
traividyā māṃ somapāḥ pūtapāpā
yajñairiṣṭvā svargatiṃ prārthayante |
te puṇyamāsādya surendraloka-
maśnanti divyāndivi devabhogān || 20 ||
verses.word_meanings: traividyāḥ—knowers of the three Vedas; mām—Me; soma-pāḥ—drinkers of the Soma juice; pūta-pāpāḥ—purified of sins; yajñaiḥ iṣṭvā—worshiping through sacrifices; svar-gatim—attainment of heaven; prārthayante—pray for; te—they; puṇyam—pious/meritorious; āsādya—reaching; surendra-lokam—the world of Indra; aśnanti—enjoy; divyān—celestial; divi—in heaven; deva-bhogān—pleasures of the gods.
verses.translation: The knowers of the three Vedas, purified of sins through Soma offerings, worship Me through sacrifices and pray for passage to heaven. Attaining the meritorious world of Indra (Surendraloka), they enjoy the celestial pleasures of the gods in heaven.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna explains the limitation of ritualistic religion. Seekers who perform Vedic rites desiring temporary heavenly delights (Svarga) do attain Indra's paradise and relish celestial joys, yet this state is temporary and fundamentally within the realm of material nature.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालं
क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति |
एवं त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्ना
गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते || २१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालं
क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति |
एवं त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्ना
गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
te taṃ bhuktvā svargalokaṃ viśālaṃ
kṣīṇe puṇye martyalokaṃ viśanti |
evaṃ trayīdharmamanuprapannā
gatāgataṃ kāmakāmā labhante || 21 ||
verses.word_meanings: te—they; tam—that; bhuktvā—having enjoyed; svarga-lokam—heavenly world; viśālam—vast; kṣīṇe puṇye—when merit is exhausted; martya-lokam—into the mortal world; viśanti—they enter; evam—thus; trayī-dharmam—the ritualistic dharma of the three Vedas; anuprapannāḥ—adhering to; gata-āgatam—coming and going (transmigration); kāma-kāmāḥ—desirers of sense desires; labhante—they attain.
verses.translation: Having enjoyed the vast celestial realm of heaven, when their merit is exhausted, they enter again into the mortal world. Thus, following the ritualistic injunctions of the three Vedas and harboring worldly desires, they achieve only transient coming and going.
verses.meaning: The tragedy of fruitive desire (Kamakama): Heavenly delights are not eternal. Once one's stock of pious karma (Punya) is spent, the soul must plummet back into the earthly sphere (Martyaloka). Those who chase finite desires through ritualism remain trapped in the endless revolving door of birth, death, and return (Gatagatam).

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते |
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् || २२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते |
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate |
teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham || 22 ||
verses.word_meanings: ananyāḥ—with undivided attention/exclusive devotion; cintayantaḥ—meditating upon; mām—Me; ye janāḥ—those persons who; paryupāsate—worship wholeheartedly; teṣām—for them; nitya-abhiyuktānām—who are constantly united with Me; yoga-kṣemam—supply of spiritual needs and preservation of possessions; vahāmi—personally carry/bear; aham—I.
verses.translation: To those who meditate on Me with undivided devotion and worship Me constantly, I personally carry what they lack and preserve what they possess (Yoga-kṣema).
verses.meaning: One of the most profound and cherished promises in all world scripture. Sri Krishna assures His surrendered devotees: Yoga is granting what the devotee lacks (spiritual enlightenment, virtues, peace), and Kshema is safeguarding what they already possess (devotion, well-being, spiritual security). The Lord Himself takes personal responsibility ('Vahamy Aham') for those whose minds are constantly absorbed in Him.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
येऽप्यन्यदेवताभक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः |
तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम् || २३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
येऽप्यन्यदेवताभक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः |
तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम् || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ye'pyanyadevatābhaktā yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ |
te'pi māmeva kaunteya yajantyavidhipūrvakam || 23 ||
verses.word_meanings: ye api—even those who; anya-devatā-bhaktāḥ—devotees of other deities; yajante—worship; śraddhayā anvitāḥ—endowed with faith; te api—they too; mām eva—Me alone; kaunteya—O son of Kunti; yajanti—worship; avidhi-pūrvakam—in an unauthorized/irregular manner.
verses.translation: Even those devotees who worship other celestial deities with sincere faith, they too worship Me alone, O son of Kunti, though in an irregular manner (Avidhipurvakam).
verses.meaning: Because the Supreme Lord is the indwelling soul of all beings and the cosmic source of all divine opulences, any genuine worship directed toward secondary deities indirectly reaches Krishna. However, worshiping the parts without recognizing the Whole is 'Avidhipurvakam'—an indirect and incomplete method that yields limited fruits.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च |
न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते || २४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च |
न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhureva ca |
na tu māmabhijānanti tattvenātaścyavanti te || 24 ||
verses.word_meanings: aham—I am; hi—truly; sarva-yajñānām—of all sacrifices; bhoktā—the enjoyer/beneficiary; ca—and; prabhuḥ eva ca—the supreme Lord also; na tu—not however; mām—Me; abhijānanti—they recognize; tattvena—in truth/essence; ataḥ—therefore; cyavanti—they fall down; te—they.
verses.translation: For I alone am the Enjoyer and Lord of all sacrifices. But because they do not recognize Me in truth, they fall down into mortal existence.
verses.meaning: Krishna is the sole recipient and supreme lord (Bhokta and Prabhu) of every sacrificial offering. When seekers fail to realize the Supreme Lord in His true essence and instead direct their devotion toward finite intermediary deities for temporary boons, they miss the ultimate goal and fall back into material transmigration.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यान्ति देवव्रता देवान्पितॄन्यान्ति पितृव्रताः |
भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् || २५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यान्ति देवव्रता देवान्पितॄन्यान्ति पितृव्रताः |
भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yānti devavratā devānpitṝnyānti pitṛvratāḥ |
bhūtāni यान्ति bhūtejyā yānti madyājino'pi mām || 25 ||
verses.word_meanings: yānti—go; deva-vratāḥ—worshipers of celestial deities; devān—to the deities; pitṝn—to the ancestors; yānti—go; pitṛ-vratāḥ—worshipers of ancestors; bhūtāni—to the spirits/elements; yānti—go; bhūta-ijyāḥ—worshipers of spirits; yānti—come; mat-yājinaḥ api—My devotees also; mām—unto Me.
verses.translation: Worshipers of celestial deities go to the deities; worshipers of the ancestors go to the ancestors; worshipers of spirits go to the spirits; and those who worship Me come unto Me.
verses.meaning: Consciousness determines destination. The focus of one's aspiration shapes one's ultimate spiritual destination. Those who dedicate their lives to mortal beings or finite deities attain finite abodes, but those who surrender their hearts in love to Sri Krishna (Madyajinah) attain His eternal, imperishable supreme domain.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति |
तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः || २६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति |
तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati |
tadahaṃ bhaktyupahṛtamaśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ || 26 ||
verses.word_meanings: patram—a leaf; puṣpam—a flower; phalam—a fruit; toyam—water; yaḥ—whoever; me—unto Me; bhaktyā—with devotion/love; prayacchati—offers; tat—that; aham—I; bhakti-upahṛtam—offered with devotion; aśnāmi—accept/partake; prayata-ātmanaḥ—of the pure-hearted soul.
verses.translation: Whoever offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or even water—that offering of love from a pure-hearted soul, I lovingly accept.
verses.meaning: One of the most tender, beautiful verses in the Bhagavad Gita. God does not demand opulent, expensive rituals, gold, or grand temples. The simplest natural offering—a humble green leaf, a wild blossom, a single piece of fruit, or a drop of clean water—when offered with sincere, heartfelt love and a purified heart (Prayatatmanah), is accepted with joy by the Supreme Lord of all universes.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् |
यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् || २७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् |
यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yatkaroṣi yadaśnāsi yadjuhoṣi dadāsi yat |
yattapasyasi kaunteya tatkuruṣva madarpaṇam || 27 ||
verses.word_meanings: yat karoṣi—whatever you do; yat aśnāsi—whatever you eat; yat juhoṣi—whatever you offer in sacrifice; dadāsi yat—whatever you give in charity; yat tapasyasi—whatever austerities you perform; kaunteya—O son of Kunti; tat kuruṣva—do that; mat-arpaṇam—as an offering unto Me.
verses.translation: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give away in charity, and whatever austerities you practice, O son of Kunti—do that as an offering unto Me!
verses.meaning: The complete spiritualization of daily life. Krishna invites Arjuna to transform every mundane and sacred moment into living worship: work, eating, charity, self-discipline, and devotion are all unified into a continuous stream of dedication to God (Mad-arpanam), dissolving the false boundary between secular and sacred.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्मबन्धनैः |
संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि || २८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्मबन्धनैः |
संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
śubhāśubhaphalairevaṃ mokṣyase karmabandhanaiḥ |
sannyāsayogayuktātmā vimukto māmupaiṣyasi || 28 ||
verses.word_meanings: śubha-aśubha-phalaiḥ—from good and evil results; evam—thus; mokṣyase—you shall be liberated; karma-bandhanaiḥ—from the fetters of action/karma; sannyāsa-yoga-yukta-ātmā—with the mind united in the yoga of renunciation; vimuktaḥ—liberated; mām—unto Me; upaiṣyasi—you shall attain.
verses.translation: Thus you shall be freed from the binding chains of karma, with its pleasant and unpleasant fruits. With your mind firmly established in this yoga of renunciation (Sannyasa Yoga), liberated, you shall come to Me.
verses.meaning: By dedicating every act to Sri Krishna, one transcends the dualities of auspicious (Shubha) and inauspicious (Ashubha) karma. This synthesis of action and renunciation (Sannyasa-yoga) severs the roots of ego-bondage, granting absolute liberation and divine union.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः |
ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् || २९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः |
ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् || २९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
samo'haṃ sarvabhūteṣu na me dveṣyo'sti na priyaḥ |
ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpyaham || 29 ||
verses.word_meanings: samaḥ—equal/impartial; aham—I am; sarva-bhūteṣu—in all living entities; na—not; me—to Me; dveṣyaḥ—hated/enemy; asti—is; na—nor; priyaḥ—favored/dear; ye—those who; bhajanti—worship; tu—but; mām—Me; bhaktyā—with devotion; mayi—in Me; te—they; teṣu—in them; ca api—and also; aham—I am.
verses.translation: I am equally present in all living beings; to Me there is neither enemy nor favorite. But those who worship Me with loving devotion abide in Me, and I also abide in them.
verses.meaning: The sun shines equally upon all surfaces, yet only a clean mirror reflects its radiant light. Similarly, Sri Krishna is impartial and all-pervading (Samo'ham sarva-bhuteshu), holding no favoritism or prejudice. But when a devotee opens their heart in sincere love, an intimate reciprocal bond of spiritual union is established: the devotee dwells in God, and God dwells in the devotee.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् |
साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः || ३० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् |
साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः || ३० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
api cetsudurācāro bhajate māmananyabhāk |
sādhureva sa mantavyaḥ samyagvyavasito hi saḥ || 30 ||
verses.word_meanings: api cet—even if; su-durācāraḥ—one of very wicked conduct; bhajate—worships; mām—Me; ananya-bhāk—with undivided devotion; sādhuḥ eva—righteous indeed; saḥ—he; mantavyaḥ—must be considered; samyak—rightly; vyavasitaḥ—resolved/determined; hi—surely; saḥ—he.
verses.translation: Even if a person of the most depraved conduct turns to Me with exclusive, undivided devotion, he must still be regarded as righteous (Sadhu), for he has rightly resolved in his spiritual determination.
verses.meaning: The supreme redeeming power of divine grace: No soul is irrevocably lost. Even one who has committed egregious moral errors, upon surrendering wholeheartedly to Sri Krishna with ananya-bhakti, has made the ultimate, correct soul-choice (Samyag vyavasito hi sah) and is regarded as a saintly soul embarking upon immediate purification.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति |
कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति || ३१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति |
कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति || ३१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kṣipraṃ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvacchāntiṃ nigacchati |
kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati || 31 ||
verses.word_meanings: kṣipram—quickly; bhavati—becomes; dharma-ātmā—a righteous/virtuous soul; śaśvat-śāntim—everlasting peace; nigacchati—attains; kaunteya—O son of Kunti; pratijānīhi—proclaim/declare boldly; na—never; me—My; bhaktaḥ—devotee; praṇaśyati—perishes/is lost.
verses.translation: Quickly he becomes a virtuous soul and attains everlasting peace. O son of Kunti, proclaim it boldly: My devotee never perishes!
verses.meaning: A lion-roar of divine assurance: 'Kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati' (O son of Kunti, proclaim it boldly: My devotee shall never perish!). Through genuine surrender, past karmic dross is incinerated, the inner nature becomes righteous (Dharmatma), and eternal peace (Shashvat Shantim) is attained.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः |
स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परमां गतिम् || ३२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः |
स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परमां गतिम् || ३२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
māṃ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye'pi syuḥ pāpayonayaḥ |
striyo vaiśyāstathā śūdrāste'pi yānti paramāṃ gatim || 32 ||
verses.word_meanings: mām—in Me; hi—indeed; pārtha—O son of Pritha; vyapāśritya—taking refuge; ye api—whoever; syuḥ—may be; pāpa-yonayaḥ—of disadvantaged/humble birth; striyaḥ—women; vaiśyāḥ—merchants; tathā—also; śūdrāḥ—laborers; te api—they too; yānti—attain; paramām gatim—the Supreme Goal.
verses.translation: For taking refuge in Me, O Partha, even those of disadvantaged birth—women, merchants, and laborers—they all attain the Supreme Goal!
verses.meaning: The radical spiritual egalitarianism of the Bhagavad Gita: Sri Krishna dismantles all social, gender, and caste barriers in the realm of devotion. Liberation is not the exclusive privilege of scholars or ascetics; anyone who takes refuge in the Supreme Lord with sincere love attains the highest spiritual destination (Paramam Gatim).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा |
अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम् || ३३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा |
अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम् || ३३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kiṃ punarbrāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣayastathā |
anityamasukhaṃ lokamimaṃ prāpya bhajasva mām || 33 ||
verses.word_meanings: kim punaḥ—how much more then; brāhmaṇāḥ—Brahmanas (spiritual seekers); puṇyāḥ—virtuous/pious; bhaktāḥ—devotees; rāja-ṛṣayaḥ—royal sages; tathā—also; anityam—transient/temporary; asukham—joyless/miserable; lokam—world; imam—this; prāpya—having obtained; bhajasva—worship/engage in devotion; mām—unto Me.
verses.translation: How much more easily then do virtuous Brahmanas and dedicated royal sages (Rajarshis) attain Me! Therefore, having obtained this transient and joyless world, engage in loving devotion unto Me!
verses.meaning: Having arrived in this ephemeral (Anitya) and sorrowful (Asukha) mortal world, one should not waste precious human life in worldly entanglements. Instead, one should turn the heart toward loving contemplation and service of the Supreme Lord.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु |
मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः || ३४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु |
मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः || ३४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru |
māmevaiṣyasi yuktvaivamātmānaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ || 34 ||
verses.word_meanings: mat-manāḥ—fixing your mind on Me; bhava—become; mat-bhaktaḥ—My devotee; mat-yājī—sacrificing unto Me; mām—unto Me; namaskuru—bow down/offer reverence; mām eva—to Me alone; eṣyasi—you shall come; yuktvā—having united; evam—thus; ātmānam—the self; mat-parāyaṇaḥ—regarding Me as the Supreme Goal.
verses.translation: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, sacrifice unto Me, bow down to Me. Having thus united your soul with Me and regarding Me as the Supreme Goal, you shall certainly come unto Me!
verses.meaning: The magnificent crowning verse of Chapter 9 (reiterated in 18.65 as the final essence of the Gita). Sri Krishna outlines the fourfold pathway of total divine surrender: 1) Man-mana bhava (Fix the thinking mind on Krishna), 2) Mad-bhakto (Surrender the feeling heart in love), 3) Mad-yaji (Dedicate all actions as sacred sacrifice), 4) Mam namaskuru (Bow the ego in humble reverence). verses.purport: The magnificent crowning verse of Chapter 9 (reiterated in 18.65 as the final essence of the Gita). Sri Krishna outlines the fourfold pathway of total divine surrender: 1) Man-mana bhava (Fix the thinking mind on Krishna), 2) Mad-bhakto (Surrender the feeling heart in love), 3) Mad-yaji (Dedicate all actions as sacred sacrifice), 4) Mam namaskuru (Bow the ego in humble reverence). One who thus lives with Krishna as the supreme goal (Mat-parayana) attains eternal union with Him without fail.
